newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba sets repo tender at unchanged 3.0 pct rate.
newsitem.headline: Buba sets repo tender at unchanged 3.0 pct rate.

text.p: The Bundesbank set a tender for 14-day securities repurchase agreements, or repos, at an unchanged fixed rate of 3.00 percent on Tuesday, signalling unchanged monetary policy.

Financial markets had speculated the Bundesbank might depart from its policy of setting fixed-rate repo tenders at 3.00 percent and allow the rate to drift higher to suport the mark. The mark has fallen sharply against the dollar and other European currencies this year.
But speculation of a repo rate move had been dampened in recent days because the dollar has eased off the eight-year high of just over 1.89 marks it reached last week.

Markets nonetheless expect the central bank to tighten its policy in coming months. Speculation of a policy change is now likely to shift to the central bank's next policy-making council meeting on August 21.

The new pact wil offset a repo pact totalling 79.4 billion marks ($42.6 billion) set at a fixed rate of 3.00 percent, which expires on Wednesday. The repo rate has been held at three percent for the last year.
